Domain knowledge decides this one, because the data are a 2×2 table of co-occurrence and the table has no information about direction. In neuropathic pain diagnosis, a pathophysiological diagnosis such as L5 radiculopathy causes a symptom such as backache. A symptom does not cause the underlying nerve-root lesion. So A is the more likely direction.

The data agree that the two labels are related. Backache appears in 336 of 7,461 patients with L L5 radiculopathy (about 4.5%) and in 195 of 8,923 without it (about 2.2%).

ANSWER: A
